papers.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations. Here we use quantum simulation to investigate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction, spanning strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. Using 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, we evolve initially localized strings with static or dynamical endpoint charges. Spatially resolved measurements reveal rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation in the string interior near the pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields. String-path occupations further probe transverse rearrangements between configurations connected by plaquette operations. Retaining separate matter and gauge degrees of freedom makes local Gauss-law constraints directly accessible for error detection. Combining these constraints with ancilla checks and noise rescaling, we measure dynamics in circuits containing up to 15 second-order Trotter steps. Our results establish quantum simulation as a practical approach to exploring nonperturbative string dynamics in two spatial dimensions, with gauge redundancy serving as an experimental resource.
papers.finding: Using a 63-qubit superconducting quantum simulation of a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory, the study finds rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields.

papers.title: Beyond the Mean Gap: What Transferred-Angle QAOA Retains on a Superconducting Processor
papers.abstract: Hardware executions of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) are often validated by comparing the device's mean cost with a simulation, a check that can miss what matters for optimization. Under global depolarization, the mean normalized gap and the floor-corrected probability of every set of bitstrings, the optimum included, retain the same fraction of their noiseless improvement over uniform sampling. We test this prediction with depth-2, transferred-angle QAOA circuits for binary subproblems of an alternating-direction decomposition on the IBM Heron processor \texttt{ibm\_marrakesh}, with and without dynamical decoupling and twirling. At 12 qubits, the main-family circuits retained 29\% to 46\% of their mean-gap improvement but only 5\% to 15\% of their probability of the optimum, lower on at least nine of ten instances per run. Near-optimal bitstrings were lost about as much as the optimum, whereas the avoidance of poor bitstrings was retained best. In the first submission, a device-matched noise model reproduced the pattern but overestimated the retention of the optimum five- to eightfold. On a rugged planted family, the device found the optimum in 62\% of 768-shot blocks (noiseless: 98\%), within the range of local heuristics. Validations of optimization circuits should report retention of the optimum and of near-optimal sets.
papers.finding: Using depth-2 QAOA circuits on the IBM Heron processor, the study finds that at 12 qubits circuits retained 29–46% of mean-gap improvement but only 5–15% of the probability of the optimum.

papers.title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule. For a representative bucket-brigade QRAM query with a $12$-qubit address register we obtain a query fidelity of $0.969$. The query consumes $3.51\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J}$ of dynamic energy, corresponding to an average dynamic power of $4.38\,\mathrm{W}$ and a peak of $64.4\,\mathrm{W}$. Our optimization shows that, at fixed target fidelity, the operating point and attenuation profile can change the average power by a factor of two or more.
papers.finding: Using the metric-noise-resource framework applied to a superconducting bucket-brigade QRAM query with a 12-qubit address register, the study finds a query fidelity of 0.969 at a dynamic energy cost of 3.51×10⁻⁴ J.

papers.title: Signs of Possible High-Temperature Superconductivity in Graphite Intercalated with Lithium-Based Alloys
papers.abstract: We report experimental results indicating possible high-temperature superconductivity in graphite intercalation compounds synthesized with lithium-based alloys. Temperature-dependent measurements of magnetic moment, trapped magnetic flux, and electrical resistance reveal transitions with critical temperatures (Tc) in the range of 240-350 K at ambient pressure, depending on the intercalation metals and synthesis conditions. The highest Tc values and largest high-Tc volume fractions (< 0.1 %) were observed in graphite samples intercalated with ternary Sr-Ca-Li alloy. Our results and analyses suggest that the observed transitions originate from local superconductivity rather than intrinsic magnetic properties of the intercalated graphite, which may be an alternative explanation. Accordingly, we propose and intend to pursue further investigations to test and confirm the nature of the observed high-Tc transitions, and to obtain larger high-Tc fractions by optimizing the intercalation materials and synthesis methods.
papers.finding: Using temperature-dependent measurements of magnetic moment, trapped flux, and resistance in lithium-alloy-intercalated graphite, the study reports possible superconductivity with critical temperatures of 240–350 K at ambient pressure.

papers.title: Flux-Activated Resonant Control of a Bosonic Quantum Memory
papers.abstract: Universal control of bosonic degrees of freedom provides a hardware-efficient route for quantum information processing with high-dimensional systems. Bosonic circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED), which leverages auxillary transmons to coherently control long-lived superconducting cavities, is well suited to this goal. However, such systems are traditionally operated in the dispersive regime, where the nearly degenerate cavity transitions prohibit the direct addressability of individual excitation levels of the bosonic mode and increase gate complexity. Here, we achieve direct oscillator control by dynamically accessing the resonant Jaynes-Cummings (JC) interactions, implemented with a hardware that integrates on-chip broadband magnetic flux delivery with a bosonic memory housed in a 3D superconducting cavity with lifetime exceeding 0.5 ms. We demonstrate deterministic preparation of Fock states and their superpositions within 100s of nanoseconds by directly climbing the JC ladder, and realise efficient arbitrary rotations between a pair of Fock states. Our resonant control scheme provides an analytical method for manipulating the entire Hilbert space of the bosonic mode at rates potentially more favourable than traditional dispersive strategies. This on-demand access to JC interactions serves as a foundational demonstration of an alternative strategy toward realising robust Fock-basis qudits and harnessing the rich dynamics of high-dimensional bosonic systems for quantum information processing.
papers.finding: Using resonant Jaynes-Cummings interactions in a bosonic cQED platform with a 3D cavity, the study finds deterministic preparation of Fock states and their superpositions within hundreds of nanoseconds.

papers.title: Thermodynamic signatures of a nearby quantum critical endpoint in UTe$_2$ under intense magnetic field
papers.abstract: Several unconventional superconducting phases have been discovered in the vicinity of metamagnetism in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe$_2$ under magnetic field. To describe the mechanism of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity, a challenge is to characterize the quantum critical magnetic properties at the metamagnetic transition. In this work, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of UTe$_2$ under magnetic fields up to 60~T applied in the crystallographic $\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{c}$ plane. Magnetization and magnetostriction experiments have been performed under magnetic fields tilted by an angle $θ\lesssim42^\circ$ from $\mathbf{b}$ toward $\mathbf{c}$. They support that a quantum critical endpoint at the field angle $θ_{QCEP}\simeq(70\pm10)^\circ$ and magnetic field $μ_0H_{QCEP}\simeq(75\pm10)$~T terminates the metamagnetic transition line. A pseudo-gap in the magnetic susceptibility is related with the metamagnetic transition observed in magnetic fields for $θ<θ_{QCEP}$. The possible relation between the quantum critical endpoint and the development of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity is discussed.
papers.finding: Using magnetization and magnetostriction experiments on UTe₂ under tilted magnetic fields up to 60 T, the study finds a quantum critical endpoint at θ_QCEP ≈ (70±10)° and μ₀H_QCEP ≈ (75±10) T terminating the metamagnetic transition line.

papers.title: Steering and Local Tunneling Signatures of Majorana Corner Modes in Altermagnetic Josephson Junctions
papers.abstract: Dynamical manipulation of Majorana zero modes and their reliable distinction from topologically trivial states remain paramount challenges in topological quantum computation. Here, we propose a phase-biased altermagnetic Josephson junction as a versatile platform for generating and controlling Majorana corner configurations. Our platform utilizes the macroscopic superconducting phase difference and the Néel-vector orientation as independent control knobs to reshape the boundary mass. This allows the spatial configuration of Majorana corner modes (MCMs) to be selected at different corners of a fixed device geometry. This spatial reconfiguration yields a control-correlated conductance response. Across these configurations, the quantized zero-bias peak appears at the contacted corner in the ideal tunneling model when an MCM is present and is suppressed when it is absent. This correlation connects phase and magnetic control of corner configurations with local tunneling readout.
papers.finding: Using a proposed phase-biased altermagnetic Josephson junction with macroscopic phase difference and Néel-vector orientation as control knobs, the study finds that Majorana corner modes can be spatially reconfigured, yielding a control-correlated quantized zero-bias conductance response at the contacted corner.

papers.title: Particle-hole asymmetry and a fluctuating pair-density-wave state in a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice
papers.abstract: Whether a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice supports robust $d$-wave superconductivity remains a central question in strongly correlated physics and in the microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity. Experiments and numerical studies reveal a pronounced particle-hole asymmetry, pointing to a delicate competition among $d$-wave superconductivity, pair-density wave (PDW), stripe, charge-density wave (CDW), and antiferromagnetic correlations. Here we combine large-scale DMRG and finite-size PEPS to study the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at low doping, $δ\leq 0.1$, while tuning the next-nearest-neighbor hopping $t'$ from the electron-like ($t'>0$) to the hole-like ($t'<0$) regime. The electron-like side supports robust, nearly uniform $d$-wave pairing, whereas decreasing $t'$ induces a period-two plaquette modulation and ultimately produces, on the hole-like side, a charge-dominated state with a strongly suppressed static pairing amplitude. DMRG calculations on open strips and squares, together with PEPS calculations on open squares up to $16\times16$ sites, support this evolution. On squares with $C_4$-symmetric Hamiltonians, both methods find that the pair correlations of the hole-like state select the plaquette momenta $(π,0)$ and $(0,π)$ and decay within a few lattice spacings, while the dominant charge-density modulation forms a bidirectional checkerboard whose period extrapolates to about $4a_0$, close to that observed in lightly doped Bi-2201. These observations establish a fluctuating plaquette PDW in the lightly doped hole-like regime, in which local pairs carry finite momentum but lack phase coherence. Our results firmly establish particle-hole asymmetry as a central organizing principle for competing pairing tendencies in the lightly doped $t$-$J$ model.
papers.finding: Using large-scale DMRG and finite-size PEPS on the square-lattice t-J model at low doping, the study finds that the electron-like regime supports robust nearly uniform d-wave pairing, whereas the hole-like regime hosts a fluctuating plaquette pair-density wave with suppressed static pairing.

papers.title: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.
papers.finding: Using seven superconducting qubits to prepare a three-electron ν=1/3 Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere and reconstruct its many-body density matrix, the study finds vortex-dressed coherence extending over larger separations than electron coherence, plus a fractional quasihole charge response.

papers.title: Chiral magnon Kerr interaction from linear and nonlinear Meissner screening in ferromagnet--superconductor bilayers
papers.abstract: Magnon Kerr interaction showing a dependence of magnon dispersion frequency on its population is a useful functionality for nonlinear and quantum magnonics; its strength and sign depend on magnetic anisotropy, bias, and mode geometry. We here propose to use a superconducting gate to tune the Kerr interaction of magnons in ferromagnetic insulators. Even when the superconductor responds linearly, the frequency shift induced by its reflected dipolar field depends on the longitudinal magnetization. The decrease of this magnetization with increasing precession amplitude therefore produces a Kerr contribution. We go beyond this linear Meissner-screening regime by showing that at finite excitation amplitude, the significant Meissner screening currents reduce the superfluid stiffness, thus enhancing the effective magnetic-field penetration and rendering the Meissner backaction amplitude dependent. This superflow-induced pair breaking adds a second Kerr contribution, controlled by the interfacial superflow relative to the nonlinear screening scale. For yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium, we predict a significant renormalization of the Kerr effect by superconductors, with the resulting Kerr contribution strongly chiral in the Damon--Eshbach configuration. By showing that the linear and nonlinear Meissner screening to the Kerr interaction can be distinguished by varying temperature, our work establishes a route to directional control of magnon nonlinear interactions.
papers.finding: Using a proposed superconducting gate to tune magnon Kerr interactions in ferromagnetic insulators, the study predicts for yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium a significant renormalization of the Kerr effect, strongly chiral in the Damon-Eshbach configuration.
